title: Run the Access Task
subtitle: Grant exactly what the role profile lists
scenario: It is SD-1. The plan says grant the new hire's access today. You do not decide what to grant - you read the role profile and grant exactly its access groups, no more. Least-privilege is enforced by sourcing access from the role, not from a request.
inputLabel: Access task (from the plan and role profile)
input: Task: access for hire H-4021 (owner Facilities Coordinator, due SD-1). Role profile access groups for Logistics Coordinator: ops-general, warehouse-readonly. Rule: grant exactly the profile's groups. Do not add extras (no admin, no finance) - a grant the profile does not list is a policy exception.
instructions: Create one row per access group the role profile lists.
Grant ops-general and warehouse-readonly - and only those.
Set grantedBy to the Facilities Coordinator on each row.
Return a JSON array of the grant rows, then validate.
copilotPrompt: Build a JSON array of access grants from the role profile. One row per access group (ops-general, warehouse-readonly), each with grantedBy. Grant only the profile's groups - do not add extras.
successMessage: Access granted. The hire has exactly the role's groups - nothing more, nothing less.
editorHelper: One row per access group the profile lists - no extras.

sections.title: Access comes from the role
sections.body: You are not deciding what this hire can reach - the role profile already did. Granting exactly its access groups is what makes access consistent and auditable across every hire in the role.

sections.title: No extras
sections.body: The temptation is to add 'just in case' access. Least-privilege says no: a grant the profile does not list is a policy exception, not a convenience, and it has to be justified separately.

sections.title: Traceable to a profile
sections.body: Because every grant points back to a role profile entry, an auditor can answer 'why does this person have this?' with 'their role grants it' - not 'someone asked once'.

sections.title: What you produce here
sections.body: A short grant list the task tracker reads. It is the access leg of four parallel branches, and it reuses the same role profile the plan expanded.

fieldGuide.meaning: An access group from the role profile.
fieldGuide.hint: Only the profile's groups: ops-general, warehouse-readonly.
The Facilities Coordinator owns the access task.

realWorld.soloRebuildPath: You'd add the person to exactly the groups their role lists in your access sheet - resisting the urge to copy a busy colleague's extra access.

tools.python: iterate the role profile's access_groups and grant each

takeaway.heading: Access granted
points: You granted exactly the role profile's groups: ops-general and warehouse-readonly.
No extras were added - least-privilege is enforced by sourcing access from the role.
Each grant traces back to a role profile entry, so access is auditable.
